body: Our family absolutely loved this movie. It was beautiful and breathtaking. It was so moving, and while biblically sound, they also used beautiful imagery and wonderfully written songs to flesh out a really tangible version of David. I had tears in my eyes multiple times and we left so inspired. We will definitely own this, and rewatch many times I'm sure.

I thought they did a really good job with this movie, the animations, and the songs. The only downfall I feel was the last third or so. It wasn't bad, it was just a little bit hard to follow since so much was put in. Overall I thought it was a great movie and I'd watch it again. Considering how the story is written in the Bible, they definitely made it flow pretty well.

I was part of the crowdfunding investors, so of course I was really hoping I would love this movie. But I didn't. At the end, I looked over to my wife and said, "I can see how they used the story of David as inspiration for this movie"... because it felt like a completely different story from what actually is in the Bible, with a few similarities that maybe link to it.

First of all, the theme of David's life in the Bible is that he's a man after God's own heart. But this movie makes David's heroism more in line with modern pacifism (David was a warrior, in fact God didn't let him build a temple because of the blood on his hands, but the movie presents David as able to solve everything peacefully), and really only references God as tangental to the story. The only place that God really seems to be impacting the story is when they have Goliath yell directly to God, which is one of the few tweaks they made to the Biblical narrative that I actually kind of liked. But even David's songs are all about an obscure "light" which may or may not point to God.

Which brings me to my next major disappointment about the movie ... David was a SONGWRITER and the Bible contains MANY, MANY songs that he wrote. One would think that maybe the filmmakers could include at least ONE song from David's actual library? The songs David actually sing in the movie, honestly, I don't think he would have approved.

I could go on with details that really bothered me. Samuel did not tell David's family why he was anointing him. The reason God rejected Saul was not because Israel would never be safe with him as king. Saul did not recognize David when he killed Goliath. David definitely did not play with an orchestra of other musicians to soothe Saul.

I could go on, but I'm going to stop here. I thought the production value was amazing. The sets were gorgeous, the sound design and music was technically wonderful. I just wish the story was actually more in line with the actual life of David.

I was in Branson this last summer and watched Sight and Sound's David musical. I think it's ironic that I saw David's story told by two different production companies within a few months of each other. Sight and Sound was much more true to the Biblical narrative and didn't add modern themes to the story. The contrast between the story they told and the one presented on screen by Angel Studios was striking.

I was hoping I would love the movie and I was so relieved that it lived up to expectations.

It walked a fine line by staying true to the Biblical account, but also remaining family-friendly and not too scary for little kids (I had a 6, 13, 15, and 17 year-old with me and they all loved it).

I appreciated the pacing and how they didn't draw out or agonize over just David and Goliath, but kept right on moving with other aspects of David's life. They covered a lot of ground and gave some nice small story arcs to smaller characters that fit in nicely overall. Jonathan's ending was beautiful and devastating (it reminded me of Finnick in the Hunger Games). I was choked up. Ditto for the ending. Such a beautiful message about fully yielding to God that was done very well.

It almost started to feel a little long in the last third, and just when I was starting to check the time, it picked up and had a fantastic climax, denouement, and ending.

Highly recommend.

The animation was excellent. The music, score, songs, singing, and were absolutely incredible and great. I even purchased the soundtrack! Love it! BUT The only thing is that David had a close and intimate relationship with God. We should have experienced that in the movie and we did not. David spoke with God and he even saw and spoke about many things in the psalms with prophetic words and even prophecy about The Messiah. There should have been more prayer spoken from David's mouth to God AND there should have been more than just a silent non-speaking light showing up on the screen with regard to the God of Israel. We should have experienced God's interaction with David and His voice. For God always spoke with David and Vice versa. David was chosen by God even before he was anointed as king. If we had seen what was missing, then I would have given this movie a perfect 10. Because this very key fact of importance which has everything to do with David's heart for God AND it Is this key information that is Missing from the movie and storyline, I gave this movie a 7 instead of a 10. I hope the next sequel includes the true interaction and intimacy between David and God. Thank you!
